scope: Selected U.S. federal AI, security, cryptography and privacy authorities. General organizations, federal agencies and defense contexts are labeled separately.
limitations: This is an applicability and evidence workbench, not a certification or exhaustive statement of law.
State, local, tribal, sector-specific, civil-rights, agency and contract rules may add obligations. Confirm scope with the responsible officials.
Links and summaries are a dated snapshot; reassess changes, exceptions, new rules and contract deviations before deployment.
Manual evidence entries are assertions, not independently validated controls.

controls.title: FIPS 203 · ML-KEM
controls.scope: All profiles; agency policy determines parameters
controls.action: Use ML-KEM for post-quantum key establishment inside an authenticated, reviewed protocol. It is not a standalone file cipher.
controls.evidence: Protocol design, parameter set, authenticated public-key distribution and interoperability evidence.
controls.appEvidence: Local evaluation key generation supports ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024; no network protocol is enabled.

controls.title: FIPS 204 · ML-DSA
controls.scope: Systems needing post-quantum signatures
controls.action: Use ML-DSA for digital signatures and identity/integrity checks, not encryption.
controls.evidence: Signing policy, key custody, verification and rotation evidence.
controls.appEvidence: Evaluation key generation supports ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87.

controls.title: FIPS 205 · SLH-DSA
controls.scope: Systems selecting hash-based post-quantum signatures
controls.action: Evaluate SLH-DSA when hash-based signatures fit the application and performance requirements.
controls.evidence: Vendor support, chosen parameter set and signature verification tests.
controls.appEvidence: Reference guidance only; this app does not generate SLH-DSA keys.

controls.title: SP 800-227 · KEM use
controls.scope: Systems integrating KEMs
controls.action: Review KEM composition, public-key authentication and key derivation. Use a maintained protocol implementation.
controls.evidence: Design review, peer authentication, key confirmation where required and negative tests.
controls.appEvidence: Key-pair self-tests verify internal consistency, not secure deployment.

controls.title: FIPS 140-3 · Module validation
controls.scope: Government cryptographic protection and contracts requiring validated modules
controls.action: Verify the exact CMVP certificate, module version, operational environment, approved services and Security Policy. An algorithm name or FIPS runtime flag is insufficient.
controls.evidence: Current certificate, applicable algorithm validations and approved-mode configuration evidence.
controls.appEvidence: This app has no verified CMVP integration. Government key generation is blocked; evaluation keys are explicitly non-validated.

controls.title: OMB M-26-15 · PQC migration
controls.scope: Covered federal information systems; excludes national security systems
controls.action: Maintain a cryptographic inventory and phased migration plan. Prioritize high-impact, high-value and long-lived sensitive systems. The memorandum calls for a plan within 120 days of June 24, 2026 and risk reduction by December 31, 2030, with later signature and remaining-system phases.
controls.evidence: Accountable owner, cryptographic inventory, risk tiers, vendor roadmaps, milestones, funding and migration tests.
controls.appEvidence: AI asset inventory can supply starting evidence; the app does not discover all cryptographic uses or submit agency plans.

controls.title: NIST IR 8547 · Transition draft
controls.scope: Migration planning; confirm final successor before decisions
controls.kind: Initial public draft, not a final standard
controls.action: Use as transition planning context alongside current binding agency policy. Do not treat a draft as a universal legal deadline.
controls.evidence: Current publication status and agency-approved migration requirements.
controls.appEvidence: Source link and planning guidance only.

controls.title: NSA CNSA 2.0 / CNSS policy
controls.scope: National security systems and contracts incorporating applicable requirements
controls.action: Consult current CNSS Policy 15, CNSA 2.0 guidance and approved products. Selecting ML-KEM-1024 or ML-DSA-87 alone does not authorize an NSS deployment.
controls.evidence: System classification, applicable NSA/CNSS requirements, approved products and authorizing-official evidence.
controls.appEvidence: No NSS, classified-system or CNSA product approval is provided.

controls.title: NIST AI RMF
controls.scope: General, federal and contractor risk management
controls.kind: Voluntary framework unless adopted by policy or contract
controls.action: Govern, map, measure and manage AI risks across the lifecycle, with accountable humans and documented decisions.
controls.evidence: Use-case inventory, impact assessment, evaluation plan, risk register and monitoring records.
controls.appEvidence: AI-BOM, red-team evidence, policies and incident records supply partial technical evidence.

controls.title: NIST AI 600-1 · Generative AI profile
controls.scope: Generative AI deployments
controls.action: Evaluate generative-AI risks including confabulation, privacy, information integrity, security and human oversight.
controls.evidence: Data provenance, model evaluations, documented limitations, monitoring and incident response.
controls.appEvidence: Synthetic injection/exfiltration tests and at-rest checks cover selected risks, not the entire profile.

controls.title: OMB M-25-21 · Federal AI use
controls.scope: Covered executive agencies; review stated exclusions
controls.action: Identify high-impact AI and apply required governance, testing, oversight and risk-management practices. Maintain agency AI inventories and accountability.
controls.evidence: CAIO/owner, high-impact determination, predeployment testing, monitoring, human oversight and required reporting.
controls.appEvidence: Inventory and technical tests are evidence inputs; the app cannot make an agency high-impact or legal determination.

controls.title: OMB M-25-22 · AI acquisition
controls.scope: Covered agency acquisition of AI; review exclusions
controls.action: Assess vendor performance, data rights, portability, interoperability and lifecycle risk in AI procurement.
controls.evidence: Contract clauses, data-use terms, acceptance criteria, vendor evidence and exit plan.
controls.appEvidence: Model/tool inventory and regression results support vendor review, not contract approval.

controls.title: OMB M-26-04 · LLM acquisition principles
controls.scope: Covered federal acquisition and use of LLMs; review open-source provisions
controls.action: Review applicable procurement provisions and due diligence for truth-seeking and ideological-neutrality principles, using the memorandum definitions.
controls.evidence: Acquisition applicability review, documented model evaluations and required contract language.
controls.appEvidence: No automated ideological-neutrality or legal certification is implemented.

controls.title: OMB M-26-05 · Software and hardware assurance
controls.scope: Federal agencies and applicable procurement terms
controls.kind: Federal agency policy; rescinds M-22-18 and M-23-16
controls.action: Use a complete inventory and risk-based supplier assurance matched to agency mission needs. Confirm current contract terms instead of treating rescinded attestation policies as mandatory.
controls.evidence: Software/hardware inventory, risk analysis, supplier assurance and contractual requirements.
controls.appEvidence: Dependency, repository, model and AI-BOM scans offer partial inventory and supply-chain evidence.

controls.title: OMB M-26-14 · Logging and network visibility
controls.scope: Covered federal systems; NSS and specified defense/IC systems excluded
controls.action: Define risk-based logging for continuous monitoring and investigation, with appropriate protections and retention.
controls.evidence: Logging strategy, selected event coverage, access control, retention, investigation and response evidence.
controls.appEvidence: Local audit chains and filesystem alerts are partial, bounded telemetry; OS permissions and routed-client coverage apply.

controls.title: FISMA / FIPS 199 and 200
controls.scope: Federal information systems within scope
controls.action: Categorize the information system and select applicable security requirements and controls through the agency process.
controls.evidence: System boundary, impact category, applicable controls and responsible officials.
controls.appEvidence: Host scans are point-in-time observations; they do not establish FISMA compliance.

controls.title: NIST SP 800-53 · Security and privacy controls
controls.scope: Selected baselines and tailored system controls
controls.action: Select and implement relevant access, audit, incident, configuration, privacy and supply-chain controls; assess effectiveness.
controls.evidence: Tailored control baseline, implementation statements, assessment results, gaps and remediation plan.
controls.appEvidence: Reports can support evidence collection but do not test all controls or replace an authorization process.

controls.title: FedRAMP · Federal cloud services
controls.scope: Cloud services processing applicable federal information
controls.kind: Federal cloud program; check current scope and rules
controls.action: Determine whether the offering falls in FedRAMP scope and review provider evidence together with agency responsibilities.
controls.evidence: Service boundary, official provider status, shared-responsibility matrix and agency authorization evidence.
controls.appEvidence: No FedRAMP certification, provider validation or agency ATO is issued by the app.

controls.title: Privacy Act of 1974
controls.scope: Applicable federal systems of records
controls.action: Determine systems-of-records applicability; review collection authority, notice, permitted disclosure and individual rights.
controls.evidence: System-of-records analysis, applicable notices, access/correction procedures and disclosure accounting.
controls.appEvidence: PII pattern scans cannot determine Privacy Act applicability or establish lawful processing.

controls.title: E-Government Act §208 · PIAs
controls.scope: Covered federal IT and identifiable information
controls.action: Determine whether a privacy impact assessment is required before new or substantially changed identifiable-information processing.
controls.evidence: Approved PIA, data-flow map, minimization, safeguards and publication/exemption decision.
controls.appEvidence: The app can record evidence references; it does not approve a PIA.

controls.title: NIST Privacy Framework
controls.scope: All organizations
controls.action: Identify data processing, purposes, privacy risks, retention, access and individual expectations.
controls.evidence: Data inventory, purpose and authority, retention/deletion plan, privacy risk review and data-flow controls.
controls.appEvidence: Secret/PII detection and opt-in encrypted capture support selected controls; no complete data inventory is guaranteed.

controls.title: HIPAA Security Rule
controls.scope: Covered entities and business associates handling ePHI
controls.action: Determine covered-entity/business-associate status and apply required administrative, physical and technical safeguards.
controls.evidence: Risk analysis, access and audit controls, agreements, incident and contingency procedures.
controls.appEvidence: Technical scan results are partial evidence; no HIPAA certification or legal determination is made.

controls.title: GLBA / FTC Safeguards Rule
controls.scope: Covered financial institutions and service-provider relationships
controls.action: Determine regulator and coverage; maintain the required information-security program and protect customer information.
controls.evidence: Program owner, risk assessment, safeguards, service-provider oversight and incident reporting process.
controls.appEvidence: Security tooling assists evidence collection but does not establish the full program.

controls.title: COPPA · Children’s privacy
controls.scope: Covered online services involving children under 13
controls.action: Assess service audience and knowledge of child users; review consent, notice, data retention, deletion and sharing obligations.
controls.evidence: Applicability analysis, parental consent/notice workflow, retention policy and third-party data-use review.
controls.appEvidence: The app does not identify user ages, obtain consent or certify a service as child-safe.

controls.title: FERPA · Student records
controls.scope: Covered educational agencies/institutions and applicable service arrangements
controls.action: Assess education-record coverage and lawful disclosures, agreements and access/correction rights.
controls.evidence: Institutional applicability, disclosure basis, vendor agreements and record-access procedures.
controls.appEvidence: At-rest scanning does not determine lawful education-record processing.

controls.title: NIST SP 800-171 · CUI
controls.scope: Nonfederal systems handling CUI under applicable agreements
controls.kind: Requirements as incorporated by contract or policy
controls.action: Protect CUI using the revision and requirements incorporated into the actual contract. Revision 3 publication does not automatically replace Revision 2 contract obligations.
controls.evidence: CUI boundary, contract revision, system security plan, assessments and remediation evidence.
controls.appEvidence: Local checks cover selected technical observations only.

controls.title: DFARS / CMMC requirements
controls.scope: Defense contracts with applicable clauses and FCI/CUI
controls.kind: Contractual requirements; check current clauses and deviations
controls.action: Resolve actual contract clauses, required assessment/status, current deviations and reporting obligations with the contracting authority. Do not assume a rollout phase or assessment level from a generic checklist.
controls.evidence: Contract and flow-down scope, applicable clauses, required assessment and incident-reporting records.
controls.appEvidence: No CMMC assessment, SPRS submission or defense-contract certification is performed.

controls.title: NIST SP 800-218A · Secure AI development
controls.scope: Developers and suppliers of generative AI/foundation models
controls.action: Apply secure development practices to AI data, model development, deployment and vulnerability response.
controls.evidence: Development controls, provenance, testing, release integrity and vulnerability response records.
controls.appEvidence: Repository/skill/model scans and CI examples support selected practices.

controls.title: NSPM-11 · National security AI
controls.scope: National-security AI uses and covered agencies
controls.action: Review the current national-security AI policy and agency-specific implementation instead of treating civilian AI guidance as sufficient.
controls.evidence: Applicable agency policy, use authorization, security evaluation and privacy/civil-liberties review.
controls.appEvidence: Reference guidance only; no classified data processing or national-security authorization is supported.
